questions.title: Newton’s law & the kinetic theory of gases

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The gravitational force is (directly) proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Any two of: the molecules are in continuous random motion; the molecules have negligible volume compared with the volume of the gas; the collisions are (perfectly) elastic; the collisions are instantaneous.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer: The gravitational force (≈10⁻⁴⁶ N) is enormously smaller than the weight of a molecule (≈mg ≈ 10⁻²⁶ N), so the assumption that there are no forces between the molecules is supported.

questions.title: The first law — an ideal gas thermodynamic cycle

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The increase in internal energy = work done on the system + thermal energy transferred to the system by heating (ΔU = q + W).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: pV = NkT (k = the Boltzmann constant), so U = (3/2)NkT

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: W = +8XY (compression — work done on the gas).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: W = −20XY (expansion — work done by the gas).

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer:
The work done during BC and DA is zero (constant volume). Over the complete cycle the change in internal energy is zero (the gas returns to A). From the first law, the net thermal energy supplied Q = −(net work done on the gas) = 20XY − 8XY
= +12XY

questions.title: Simple harmonic motion & heavy damping — steel ball in oil

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: The graph is a straight line through the origin, showing a is proportional to x, and its negative gradient shows a is always in the opposite direction to x — so the oscillations are simple harmonic.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
a₀ = ω²x₀ and ω = 2π/T, so T = 2π√(x₀/a₀) = 2π√(1.2/13)
= 1.9 s

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Damping is the loss of energy from the oscillations due to resistive forces.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: A line starting at x = ±1.2 cm at t = 0 (entirely above or below the t-axis), with both the magnitude of x and the magnitude of the gradient continuously decreasing — heavy damping, so the ball returns to equilibrium without oscillating.

questions.title: Hydrogen energy levels — line spectra & photon energies

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Any three of: an electron moving between levels emits a single photon; the energy of the photon equals the difference between the energy levels; the photon energy depends on frequency (E = hf); the spectrum has discrete frequencies, so the differences between electron energies (and hence the levels themselves) must be discrete.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
n = 2 level = −13.6 + 10.2 = −3.4 eV.
n = 3 energy difference = 12.1 eV, so n = 3 = −13.6 + 12.1 = −1.5 eV.
n = 4 energy difference = 12.8 eV, so n = 4 = −13.6 + 12.8 = −0.8 eV.
